page.layout: One page of text, with a full-width heading above a single column of running text. No margin notes or footnotes. The left edge of the scan is cropped, so the first letters of some lines are missing.

main_text.head: XXI. De Epistolis Regiis interceptis, & evulgatis.
main_text.p: Literas meas fuisse interceptas, opportuna erat Hostium Malitiæ, & præter spem occasio, quâ tamen honestè & civiliter uti ignorabant. Nec sane arbitror, apud æquos & probos æstimatores quicquam in illis repertum itâ mihi in probrum cessisse, quam sic turpiter fuisse divulgatas, in eorum infamiam.

Tunc enim maximè se probat virtus, generosi animi vera indoles, cùm in hostes maximè liceat, nec ullâ magis humanitate afficimur, quàm quæ ab iis defertur[?] à quibus minimum speravimus. Hanc à me gratiam inire poterant chartas meas celando: in quibus cum essent veriora quædam, atque etiam arcana, certè[?] aliquid hîc civilitatis necessarium duissent homines non plane Barbari: Nec vera quicquam unquam inhumanius factum.

page.notes: Left edge cropped: the opening letters of several lines (for example "ho-", "æsti-", "mihi", "turpi-", "hostes", "dissent") are cut off and restored from the hyphenation at line ends. The drop cap "L" is joined to the italic word "Literas". "defertur" has its initial letter cut; "certè" is a guess from a cropped line end and is marked [?]. The Roman numeral in the heading is cut at the left edge and read as XXI. The line "aliquid hîc civilitatis necessarium du-" has its continuation cut off, so "dui…ssent" is the hyphenated word, and the cut letters are not reliable; it should be checked against the original. The running head Greek is copied as printed.
